title: Enterprise Inference Winbook: Positioning, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Maya K. Torres
body:
Purpose and scope

This winbook is a single-page reference for Redwood Inference account teams engaging enterprise prospects. It contains: concise positioning and messaging, a competitive brief with battlecards, pragmatic pricing guidance and a short TCO example, a compact customer case study, and a vetted security FAQ tailored for enterprise RFPs.

Use cases and target buyer personas

- Primary buyers: Platform/Architecture leads, ML/AI engineering managers, and Product infra owners at mid-market and enterprise SaaS companies.
- Typical technical requirements we win on: predictable p95 latency, throughput at 50–200 reqs/sec for multi-tenant features, hard data residency controls (VPC/on-prem), and audit-grade logging.
- Business sponsors: Head of Product (reduce latency and costs), CTO (platform consolidation), Compliance/Legal (data residency and controls).

Elevator pitches (short + extended)

- Short (30s): "Redwood Inference gives engineering teams consistent, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — optimizing latency, cost, and reliability so you can ship features without building an infra team."

- Extended (1–2 min): "Many teams start with an open model or hosted API but hit a painful inflection when their product requires predictable latency, lower unit cost, and enterprise controls. Redwood offers a unified runtime and operations surface: hosted API for fast time-to-value; Dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput; and Private/VPC or on-prem installs for regulated workloads. We bring versioned deployments, canary rollouts, token-level cost visibility, and fallbacks to keep features online — so teams don’t re-implement serving, caching, or routing logic."

Core value pillars (talking points)

1) Production economics and predictability
- Convert variable cloud spend into predictable unit economics with Dedicated pools and autoscaling policies.
- Token-level telemetry and per-route cost dashboards to rapidly identify cost drivers.

2) Unified interface across environments
- Same API and rollout primitives in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Reduces engineering toil and risk when moving from pilot to scale.

3) Reliability and graceful degradation
- Smart routing, model fallbacks, and cache/ batch policies that protect your SLOs during spikes.

4) Enterprise controls and compliance
- VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and deployable on-prem packages for high-regulation customers.

Competitive positioning and battlecards

Competitors to emphasize: major cloud vendor managed endpoints, pure-play LLM API providers, and self-built inference stacks.

Quick matrix (high level)

| Dimension | Redwood | Cloud-managed endpoints (BigCloud) | LLM API provider (APICo) | Self-hosted stack |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Time to MVP | Fast (hosted API) | Fast | Fast | Slow |
| Predictable throughput | Dedicated pools, SLA | Variable | Variable | Depends on ops |
| Private deployment | VPC & on-prem | Limited | Rare | Yes, but costly |
| Observability | Token-level, per-route | Basic | Limited | Custom |
| Cost control | Batching, cache, quantization guidance | Few levers | Limited | Complex |
| Enterprise SLAs | Yes | Varies | Rare | Depends |

Battlecard: objection handling

- "We can just use BigCloud’s model endpoints."
  - Response: BigCloud is convenient for pilots; Redwood differentiates on predictable throughput (Dedicated), token-level cost visibility, and out-of-the-box fallback policies. For enterprise customers with strict SLOs or data residency needs, Redwood shortens time-to-production while controlling unit economics.

- "Our security team requires on-prem."
  - Response: Redwood Private supports a fully customer-controlled control plane and an on-prem package. We provide KMS/HSM integrations, audit-log exports, and a documented day-2 ops runbook. Reference: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops.

- "We already built an internal serving layer."
  - Response: Many teams start internal but face ramp costs around continuous batching, KV cache efficiency, cross-model fallbacks, and predictable kernel selection across hardware. Redwood can be deployed privately or as Dedicated with the same API, letting teams keep custom tooling while shedding the heavy operational burden.

Pricing guidance (practical rules of thumb)

- Hosted API: Best for pilots and low-volume production. Example benchmark pricing (example list price; actual pricing is contract-dependent):
  - Generation (small-medium models): $0.004 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.006 per 1k completion tokens.
  - Embeddings: $0.0008 per embedding (128-d baseline).

- Dedicated: Commit-based monthly pricing. Typical ranges (example):
  - Small pool (1–2 GPUs): $12k–$20k/month reserved.
  - Medium (4 GPUs): $40k–$65k/month reserved.
  - Pricing includes baseline throughput; overage and burst credits negotiated.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): Platform license + deployment fee + support. Typical structure: one-time deployment onboarding fee (e.g., $60k–$150k), annual platform license (100k+), and optional premium support.

TCO example (3-year view)

Assumptions: mid-market SaaS product with 10M monthly tokens processed for features, target p95 latency <200ms, and requirement for VPC.

| Option | Year 1 cost | Year 2 cost | Year 3 cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Build self-hosted | $450k | $350k | $300k | Includes hiring 1.5 FTE infra + infra spend + ops overhead |
| Redwood Private (license) | $220k | $120k | $120k | Year 1 includes onboarding; Years 2–3 platform + support |
| Cloud-managed endpoints | $180k | $200k | $220k | Higher per-token operating cost and less predictability |

Guidance: For most enterprise teams with compliance needs and non-trivial throughput, Redwood Private or Dedicated becomes cost-advantaged within 12–18 months once you factor in engineering time and reliability risk.

Pitch deck talking points (slide-by-slide guidance)

1) Problem slide: inconsistent inference economics, manual model ops, outage risk under burst.
2) Redwood solution: unified runtime + deployment modes + observability.
3) Evidence: performance profiles (p95 latency targets, per-token cost improvements up to 3x vs naive hosting).
4) Enterprise controls: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit exports, RBAC.
5) Pricing and deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private.
6) Customer outcomes: reduced latency, improved cost per token, simplified rollouts.
7) Ask: pilot with hosted API (2–4 weeks) or Dedicated POC (8–12 weeks).

Demo checklist (technical win criteria)

To qualify a deal during demo/POC:
1) Baseline p95 latency for 512-token generation <200ms target on Dedicated testbed.
2) Throughput sustained at customer target (e.g., 100 reqs/sec) with <2% error rate.
3) Token-level cost dashboard visible and instrumented.
4) Audit log export to S3/GCS and KMS integration demonstrated.
5) Canary release showing model rollback within 2 minutes.

Customer case study (short) — "AtlasOps: chat assistance for enterprise SaaS" (anonymized)

Context: AtlasOps (mid-market SaaS) shipped a contextual chat assistant for admins. They needed predictable latency (p95 < 250ms), data isolation, and predictable monthly spend.

What we did: Deployed Dedicated GPU pool (4x A100-equivalent), enabled prefix caching and KV cache sharing for conversation reuse, and set up token-level dashboards and alerts.

Outcome: Reduced median latency from 340ms -> 120ms, cut per-conversation token cost by 37% through batching and config recommendations, and replaced a proposed 2.0 FTE hiring plan to manage ops.

Security & compliance FAQ (prospect-facing, concise answers)

Q: How do you support data residency and VPC requirements?
A: Redwood Private provides a customer-controlled control plane and VPC deployments. For Hosted customers we offer region pinning and data isolation contracts. See on-prem reference architecture: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures.

Q: Do you integrate with KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys?
A: Yes. We support standard KMS providers for envelope encryption, and can integrate with HSM-backed keys for customers needing FIPS-compliant key management.

Q: How are logs and audit trails exported?
A: Audit logs are available for export to S3/GCS and can be streamed to customer SIEMs (Splunk/Datadog). We include request/response metadata, not raw PII by default; raw payload logging is configurable under customer agreement.

Q: What certifications or evidence can you provide?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II and provide compliance evidence packages for enterprise diligence. For regulated workloads we provide architecture and data flow diagrams and collaborate on pen tests under NDA.

Q: What is your incident notification and SLA process?
A: For Dedicated and Hosted with SLAs, we provide a 24x7 incident channel, initial response within 60 minutes for Sev1, and a documented post-incident review. Private customers can opt into SRE runbook alignment and playbook exchange.

Legal & procurement signals (what to watch for in RFPs)

- Red flags that increase risk: mandatory raw payload retention without encryption, a requirement for unlimited on-prem deployment customization, or compliance demands for unique certifications not in our roadmap.
- Helpful signals: requests for a POC, willingness to sign a standard addendum for data processing, and clear throughput/latency targets.

Recommended sales motions and next steps

1) Discovery: map technical SLOs (p95 latency, throughput), compliance constraints, and data residency needs. Capture these in the opportunity playbook.
2) Technical touch: propose hosted pilot for feature validation or Dedicated POC when predictable throughput is critical.
3) Procurement & legal: surface standard contract addenda (DPA, SOC2 evidence) early.
4) Success criteria: set measurable POC goals (latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens) and sign a joint-runbook before kickoff.

Appendix: recommended thresholds and internal owners

- Typical enterprise thresholds: p95 latency target <= 200ms (generation, 512 tokens), error rate < 1%, availability 99.9% for Dedicated.
- Internal owners to loop in: Solutions Engineering (owner: Priya Desai), Security & Compliance (owner: Ethan Wang), Customer Success (owner: Liam O'Connor).
